paper.title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling
paper.central_claim: Building an offline replay environment lets an explorer LLM (Claude Code) iteratively synthesize width-depth test-time-scaling controllers as code using scaling-curve and execution-trace feedback and a single beta knob; the discovered controller improves the accuracy-cost tradeoff over handcrafted TTS baselines, generalizes to held-out benchmarks/model scales, and costs only $39.9 and 160 minutes to find.

evidence.quote: However, existing TTS strategies are largely hand-crafted: researchers manually design reasoning patterns and tune heuristics by intuition, leaving much of the computation-allocation space unexplored.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: TTS controllers are hand-designed; the claim that the allocation space is unexplored is asserted, not measured.

evidence.quote: no prior work has formulated it as an algorithmic search problem.
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty claim over TTS design; nearest discovery neighbors (FunSearch, EoH, AlphaEvolve, ADAS, Meta-Harness, TTT-Discover) are cited but not run.

evidence.quote: further advances this paradigm by exposing full execution histories to the proposer, enabling targeted diagnosis of failure modes rather than relying on scalar feedback alone.
evidence.support_explanation: Trace-feedback design follows Meta-Harness; the new parts are the TTS replay environment and beta parameterization.

evidence.quote: To address this, we construct an offline replay environment that moves all LLM calls prior to the discovery process, making controller evaluation deterministic and cheap.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation substrate: pre-collected trajectories and probe signals; no live-LLM validation of replay is reported.

evidence.quote: each round, an explorer LLM (Claude Code) reads the accumulated history
evidence.support_explanation: History H holds all proposed controller implementations, accuracy-cost outcomes and execution traces; explorer model version is not given.

evidence.quote: For each round, we sweep across multiple betas and record the resulting scaling curve as the scalar component; the trajectory component then supplies fine-grained behavioral evidence, enabling the agent to diagnose failure modes and propose a more targeted controller in the next round.
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback signal = beta-sweep scaling curve + decision traces.

evidence.quote: The discovery loop runs for five rounds with Claude Code as the agent, and the final controller is selected as the one achieving the highest accuracy on
evidence.support_explanation: Selection rule: highest accuracy on the AIME24 search environments (accuracy only); single discovery run of five rounds.

evidence.quote: is fixed and evaluated on held-out environments from AIME25 and HMMT25, which are never used during discovery or selection.
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out benchmark separation claim (30 problems each).

evidence.quote: we pre-sample 128 reasoning trajectories per (model, problem) pair at temperature 0.7 with a probing interval of 500 tokens to construct the replay matrix.
evidence.support_explanation: Replay matrix size and probe granularity.

evidence.quote: each controller is evaluated 64 times independently by randomly sampling a subset of trajectories from the pre-sampled pool of 128, and the results are averaged.
evidence.support_explanation: Variance reduction over trajectory resampling; no spread across draws or across discovery runs is reported.

evidence.quote: We follow the original setting with threshold 0.95
evidence.support_explanation: Handcrafted baselines (SC@64, ASC, ESC, Parallel-Probe) run with original settings; no baseline tuning on the AIME24 search set at matched effort.

evidence.quote: outperforming all handcrafted baselines in three out of four models on average, and remaining competitive on Qwen3-8B (62.7 vs. 62.8 for SC@64).
evidence.support_explanation: Headline held-out claim at beta=1.0; accuracy margins are small except Qwen3-1.7B.

evidence.quote: it reduces token consumption by approximately 69.5% compared to SC@64 while maintaining on-par accuracy on average across all four models (45.3 vs. 45.2)
evidence.support_explanation: Token saving is quoted against SC@64, the most expensive baseline, not against ASC.

evidence.quote: resulting in a drastic token reduction (575.5K to 93.3K) accompanied by an accuracy drop from 53.1 to 49.0 on held-out benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: w/o beta ablation moves the controller to a very different operating point (6x fewer tokens), so it is not an iso-cost comparison; single discovery run.

evidence.quote: Without this, the discovered controller achieves worse performance while allocating much more tokens.
evidence.support_explanation: w/o execution traces: avg acc 51.6 vs 53.1 and tokens 824.3K vs 575.5K; single run each.

evidence.quote: Overall, the five-round discovery process costs only $39.9 and takes 160 minutes, suggesting that our replay-based discovery framework is practical to run.
evidence.support_explanation: Discovery cost; the cost of pre-sampling 128 trajectories per (model, problem) is not included in the figure.

evidence.quote: In settings where probing is treated as free relative to generation, we set
evidence.support_explanation: Probe cost kappa_probe can be zero; probe answers are precomputed. Probe-based methods (AutoTTS, Parallel-Probe) benefit relative to full-read ASC/ESC if real probing costs tokens.

evidence.quote: We report both task accuracy and tokens that measure the total number of tokens consumed across all used branches.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost metric = total generation tokens over used branches.

evidence.quote: These results suggest that the discovered strategies are not tightly overfitted to the main Qwen-based math setting, and can transfer to both a different model family and a non-math reasoning benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2: one extra model/benchmark pair (R1-Distill-Llama-8B on HMMT25) and one extra benchmark (Qwen3-1.7B on GPQA-Diamond), one run each.

evidence.quote: Additionally, the discovery process currently relies on a frontier coding agent; exploring whether open-source coding agents can achieve comparable discovery performance is an interesting direction for future work.
evidence.support_explanation: Discovery depends on a single frontier explorer; no explorer or seed variation.

evidence.quote: With only five discovery rounds, navigating this high-dimensional space causes the agent to collapse onto extreme solutions
evidence.support_explanation: Motivation for beta: agents proposed up to 10 hyperparameters; supported anecdotally by preliminary experiments and the w/o beta row.

evidence.quote: that would be difficult to arrive at through manual intuition alone.
evidence.support_explanation: Claim about the discovered Confidence Momentum Controller; no human-expert or tuned-handcrafted comparison supports it, and the code derives 12 internal hyperparameters from beta.

evidence.quote: at the start of every round, so your patch must be self-contained within
evidence.support_explanation: Each round restarts from the template and reads prior rounds from history; the history is a raw archive of code, CSV results and traces rather than a distilled memory.

Our reading of Table 1: against ASC, the discovered controller is dominated on Qwen3-4B, trades accuracy for tokens on 8B, and clearly wins only on 0.6B/1.7B; the strongest gain is +6.3 points on Qwen3-1.7B vs SC@64.

evidence.quote: Search cost ($): Ours 39.9; w/o Beta Parameterization 46.4; w/o Execution Traces 30.9; accuracy avg 53.1 / 49.0 / 51.6
evidence.support_explanation: Our reading of Table 3: ablations are single discovery runs; the 1.5-point gap for traces is within what stochastic discovery could produce, and w/o beta differs mostly in operating point.

evidence.quote: while the right panel reports the corresponding performance on the held-out AIME25 and HMMT25 benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors tracked held-out performance per round for analysis, although held-out sets are stated not to drive selection.

signatures.object: Code-defined width-depth TTS controller (OptimalController class with beta schedule and trace hooks) for a frozen base LLM; baseline = handcrafted ASC/ESC/Parallel-Probe/SC@64
signatures.information: Explorer sees the environment API, seed baselines, full history of prior controllers, their beta-sweep scaling curves and per-question decision traces; replay environment hides gold answers from the controller; controllers see probe answers only when probing
signatures.operation: Explorer LLM (Claude Code) rewrites the controller from a template each round after reading history; controller evaluated on offline replay of AIME24 for four Qwen3 models
signatures.output: Executable controller class + beta-to-hyperparameter map; final = highest AIME24 accuracy over rounds and beta
signatures.conditions: pre-sampled 128 trajectories per (model, problem), 500-token probe interval, 64 resampled evaluations per controller, 5 rounds
signatures.feedback: accuracy-token scaling curve across beta sweep; execution traces of branch/probe/prune/stop decisions
signatures.selection_rule_data: highest accuracy on search environments (AIME24); held-out AIME25/HMMT25 not used (author claim); no population, no parent sampling
signatures.persistence: history archive of rounds (code, CSV results, JSONL traces); final controller released as code
signatures.later_use: fixed controller run on held-out benchmarks and other models via replay
signatures.claimed_effect: average held-out token saving about 69.5% vs SC@64 at on-par accuracy (beta=0.5); peak accuracy beyond handcrafted in 5 of 8 cases (beta=1.0)
signatures.failure_boundary: single discovery run, one frontier explorer, replay fidelity unvalidated, probing treated as cheap, only width-depth action set

signatures.object: Search space parameterization: each controller exposes one monotone scalar beta mapped to all internal hyperparameters
signatures.operation: Discovery prompt requires single-knob schedule; map produced by the coding agent
signatures.output: 1-D sweep that traces an accuracy-cost frontier
signatures.conditions: controller must be expressible with a monotone beta schedule
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o beta: 6x fewer tokens, held-out acc 49.0 vs 53.1
signatures.failure_boundary: discovered CMC still has 12 internal hyperparameters via hand-chosen linear schedules; no iso-cost comparison

gap.author_gap: TTS strategies are hand-designed heuristics tuned by intuition; evaluating candidate strategies online is too expensive for automated search, and scalar feedback does not tell the explorer why a controller fails.
gap.checked_gap: Real but partly generic: hand-designed controllers exist, and expensive evaluation is a concrete bottleneck that replay addresses. Not established: that LLM-agent code search finds better controllers than a cheap automated tuning of the existing controllers on the same replay data; that baseline hyperparameters were optimal; that the space is meaningfully unexplored.

claims.text: Discovered controller improves the accuracy-cost tradeoff over handcrafted TTS baselines on held-out benchmarks
claims.setting: Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B/4B/8B, replay of AIME25 and HMMT25 (30 problems each)
claims.baseline_control: SC@64, ASC, ESC, Parallel-Probe at original settings
claims.result_denominator: avg held-out: beta=1.0 acc 24.6/40.6/60.5/62.7 vs best baseline 24.1/34.3/60.4/62.8; beta=0.5 tokens ~254k-379k vs SC@64 ~0.9-1.2M
claims.counterevidence: ASC dominates on Qwen3-4B and is close on 8B in token cost; margins of 0.1-0.5 acc points are inside noise on 30 problems; baselines untuned.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Discovered controller is competitive with strong baselines and clearly better than SC@64 on tokens; superiority over best handcrafted is shown only for small models.

claims.text: Discovered strategies generalize to held-out benchmarks and other model families
claims.setting: R1-Distill-Llama-8B on HMMT25; Qwen3-1.7B on GPQA-Diamond
claims.result_denominator: 27.2 vs 26.7 acc at 533.9K vs 985.7K tokens; GPQA 41.6 vs 41.3 at 151K vs 510K
claims.counterevidence: One model-benchmark pair each, tiny accuracy deltas, no repeats.
claims.allowed_conclusion: No evidence of failure out of distribution; weak evidence of transfer.

claims.text: Beta parameterization and execution traces are needed for effective discovery
claims.counterevidence: Different operating points, single run, no search-cost-matched comparison.

claims.allowed_conclusion: Agent-API cost of the loop is small; total pipeline cost not shown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A Claude Code-written controller selected on AIME24 replay achieves, on replayed AIME25/HMMT25, roughly 40-70% fewer tokens than SC@64 with on-par accuracy (author-reported), and beats the handcrafted baselines on accuracy for the 0.6B and 1.7B models.
assessment.not_supported: Superiority over tuned or ASC-style cost-efficient baselines on 4B/8B; benefit of agentic search over simpler automated tuning; fidelity of replay to live generation including probe cost; reproducibility across discovery runs; total pipeline cost.
assessment.note: Author-reported results only. Improver level not claimed: the explorer is not improved.

G.reason: Real bottleneck in expensive evaluation of adaptive allocation policies and a clear lineage to Meta-Harness/ADAS/AlphaEvolve, but the hand-crafted-heuristics gap is generic, the 'unexplored space' is not characterized, and the most relevant alternative (automated tuning of existing controllers) is not considered.

M.reason: Replay MDP, trace-augmented history and single-knob schedule form a coherent, reconstructable answer to cost and overfitting; beta's anti-overfit mechanism is asserted from preliminary observation and the schedule itself fans out to 12 hand-set hyperparameters.

X.reason: Prompt, environment API, replay setup, selection rule, final controller code and schedule are disclosed; no admission gate beyond search accuracy, explorer version/seed and beta grid unspecified, per-round template reset, and no versioning/rollback beyond a history archive.

E.measurement.reason: Accuracy vs ground truth is sound but on 30-problem sets; cost counts generation tokens only with probing treated as free; replay fidelity to live generation and probe-answer extraction cost are unvalidated; token headline is against the most expensive baseline.

E.causality.reason: Component ablations (beta, traces) exist but are single-run and not iso-cost; baselines untuned; no non-LLM search or history-off control; ASC dominance on 4B/8B undermines the tradeoff claim.

E.holdout.reason: Search on AIME24, evaluation on AIME25/HMMT25 stated as never used for selection, plus another model family and GPQA; held-out benchmarks are near-distribution to AIME24 and authors tracked held-out curves per round.

E.statistics.reason: 64 resampled evaluations are averaged but no spread, CI or significance is reported; one discovery run per variant; margins of a few tenths of a point on 30 problems.

E.cost.reason: Discovery API cost and wall-clock reported, ablation search costs given and inference tokens central, but offline pre-sampling cost and live probing cost are omitted and baseline effort is not matched.

status.reason: Complete HTML full text including discovery prompt and discovered code read; figures not available as text.

rationale: 回放环境+轨迹反馈+β单旋钮使TTS控制器发现便宜，AIME25/HMMT25留出较干净；但基线未调参(ASC在4B/8B占优)、单次发现、无方差、探针成本按免费，评scoped retained。
